method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; a dates module (rtw-dates.l4, built-in date functions only), a seat-neutral core (rtw-core.l4, with 18 regulative rules for the duties of the worker and the employer) and two seat layers (rtw-seat.l4 for the injured worker and dependants, rtw-seat-employer.l4 for the employer) that restate no rule; no REFUSE (a case the text does not answer returns an explicit not-covered value, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate. Corrected on 2026-10-24 after an independent verification (NOTES.md, "Verification of 24 October 2026").
edition_encoded: Return to Work Act 1986 (NT), reprint REPR050, as in force at 25 March 2024, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/Return-to-Work-Act-1986-NT-current-reprint-REPR050.txt; with the Return to Work Regulations 1986 (NT), reprint REPR050R2, as in force at 1 July 2024, as deposited at ../../../return-to-work-regulations-1986/registers/source-bundle/Return-to-Work-Regulations-1986-NT-current-reprint-REPR050R2.txt. The Act's reprint is more than a year old and the register's history was not checked.

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run rtw-dates.l4 ; l4 run rtw-core.l4 ; l4 run rtw-seat.l4 ; l4 run rtw-seat-employer.l4 ; l4 run rtw-cases-core.l4 ; l4 run rtw-cases-worker.l4 ; l4 run rtw-cases-employer.l4
checks.result: 380 assertions satisfied (246 core, 70 worker seat, 64 employer seat including 32 mirror cases), 0 errors, 0 warnings (2026-10-24); 25 #TRACEs with an expect line (22 breaches, 3 obligations or permissions still open), each read and as expected
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: Who is covered: s 3(1) (average weekly earnings, Territory worker), s 3A, s 3B(1)-(6), (10), (11), (14), (15), (17) with regs 3A, 4, 4A, 5, s 4 (as a fact, with s 4(2A)), s 53(1), (2), s 53AA(1), (3), s 57, s 58 (as a fact), s 60. Weekly payments: s 49A, s 64, s 65(1)-(3A), (6)-(14), s 65(1BA), (1D), s 61A(2)(a), s 65A, s 65B with reg 6A, s 61B. Lump sums and death: ss 70, 71, 72(3), (5), s 62 with regs 6, 6AA, s 63. s 74. Claims and decisions as regulative rules and deadlines: s 80, s 82(1), (2), (6) with reg 12, s 84(1), (3), (5), s 85(1)-(4), (6)(c), (8)-(10) with reg 13, ss 85A, 86, 87, 88, s 89 (weeks late only) with reg 14, s 65C, s 69(1), s 75B. Disputes: s 103D(1A), (4), (5), s 103J, s 104(3), (4), s 182 (as a regulative rule too). Out: Parts 2-3 and 7 (Authority, Council, inspectors, insurance, premiums, Nominal Insurer and Fund), s 50A firefighters and the prescribed-disease lists beyond a fact, volunteers, labour hire, sailors, ss 52-56, 61, 64(6), 65(4), 68, the rest of s 69, s 72A, s 73, Division 4 except s 75B, ss 78A-78B settlements, ss 90-92, Court procedure, transitional Parts, s 61A(2)(b)(ii). Inputs: average weekly earnings, indexed normal weekly earnings (s 65(3A) formula missing), s 89 interest (formula missing; reg 14 rate), future pension age (Social Security Act 1991 (Cth) s 23), normal retiring age, weekday public holidays, penalty unit value. Read with subjects/au/social-security-act-1991/encodings/baseline-2026-10/ (pension age; Part 3.14 compensation recovery), subjects/au/nt/motor-accidents-compensation-act-1979/ (s 10A) and subjects/au/nt/victims-of-crime-assistance-act-2006/ (s 18); cross-folder IMPORT is not possible.
seats: the injured worker (and, on a death, the worker's dependants and the person who pays for the funeral)
the employer, read with its insurer, or the Nominal Insurer if the employer is uninsured (s 85(10))
